name: Yukon
summary_text: No territory-specific trans statute, incident series or policing pattern was found for Yukon in the country dossier: the national criminal law, the national self-declaration gender framework and national protections apply directly. The one territory-level figure on record is lethal gendered violence: in 2021 the three territories together recorded 3.20 gender-related homicides per 100,000 women and girls, roughly triple the highest provincial rate (1.03), with rural areas running more than 2.5x urban rates — not trans-specific, and the only official territorial rate data available. Nationally, police-reported hate crimes targeting gender identity or expression rose 8% to 139 in 2024, a fourth consecutive annual increase and nearly triple the 2020 level (+184%), while Pride-season June saw roughly double the monthly average of incidents targeting sexual orientation.

sources.title: The Daily — Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024
sources.claim_summary: Statistics Canada release 'Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024' (published 30 March 2026): police reported 4,882 hate crimes in 2024 (+1% on 2023; +169% since 2018; rate 11.9 per 100,000). Hate crimes targeting gender identity or expression rose 8% to 139 — a fourth consecutive yearly increase and +184% since 2020; incidents targeting sexual orientation fell 26% to 658, though June (2024: 113 incidents) runs more than double the ~50-incident monthly average. Police-reported hate crime rates are ~2.5x higher in large metropolitan areas (13.9 per 100,000) than in smaller towns (5.5), which bears on sparsely-populated territories where reporting infrastructure is thinner.
